sentences: I inspect the expansion joints on the north span every Monday morning before traffic peaks.
I measure the clearance between the girder bottom and the pier cap with a folding ruler.
I check the torque on the anchor bolts at each bearing location using a calibrated wrench.
I record the water level on the pier scour gauge after every heavy rainstorm in the spring.
I paint the steel railing along the pedestrian walkway with a roller and gray primer.
I walk the full length of the deck to note any new cracks in the asphalt surface.
I tighten the bolts on the approach slab's metal expansion joint cover plate with a socket.
I sweep dirt and leaves from the bridge deck drains so rainwater can flow off the roadway.
I lower a camera on a rope to photograph the underside of the concrete box girder.
I test the strain gauges on the main suspension cables and log the readings in a notebook.
I count the number of trucks over ten tons that cross the bridge during a two-hour period.
I climb the access ladder to the top of the tower and check the aviation warning light.
I mix grout and pour it into the gap between the bearing plate and the concrete pedestal.
I review the as-built drawings to find the location of the utility conduit inside the bridge deck.
I install a temporary barrier on the sidewalk so pedestrians do not walk near the open deck joint.
I measure the vertical clearance under the bridge with a laser rangefinder from a boat on the river.
I replace the worn elastomeric bearing pad under the steel girder using a hydraulic jack.
I take photos of the riprap around the pier to document any movement of the stones after a flood.
I apply a rust converter to the corroded spot on the truss member before painting it.
I check the tension on the diagonal cable stays by reading the load cell display at the anchorage.
